digest.en: Iran struck a U.S. air base in Kuwait while Bangladesh deployed paramilitary forces against Hasina. Xi framed China as Asia's open door in APEC remarks. The EU's Ukraine funding faces a budget crossfire.

articles.title: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary as unrest grows over Hasina's return
articles.summary: Bangladesh deployed paramilitary units as unrest intensified following Sheikh Hasina's return. Police reported dozens of crude bomb blasts and vehicle arsons across 28 districts in ten days. Several officers and civilians were injured in the escalating violence. Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported.

articles.title: Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027
articles.summary: Saudi and Yemeni forces are reorganizing to prepare for a Houthi conflict extending into 2027. The coalition plans to defend Aden from Houthi advances. They also aim to shift offensive operations to eastern fronts where they have held their lines. Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines.

articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea are amassing forces along their shared border, raising fears of a wider war. Tigray fighting has stoked regional instability. Ethiopia accused Sudan and Egypt of backing rebels, though both nations denied the claims. The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.summary: Trump's Board of Peace criticized Israel and Hamas for failing to end the Gaza war. The ceasefire halted major fighting but the broader plan stalled. Hamas disarmament, Israeli troop withdrawal, and reconstruction efforts have effectively stopped. While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year.

articles.title: Ukraine Wrecked Putin's Bridge. Now It Can Choke Russian Supplies To Crimea
articles.summary: Ukraine destroyed the $4 billion Crimean Bridge, cutting road traffic between the Russian mainland and the peninsula. The damage severely strains Moscow's ability to supply the Black Sea region. Kyiv's strike targets a key Kremlin infrastructure asset. For eight years, it’s stood as a symbol of the Kremlin’s claim to Crimea: a $4 billion bridge directly linking the Russian mainland with the Ukrainian peninsula.

articles.title: RFE/RL Visits Ukraine's Newly Liberated Territory After Operation Vivaldi
articles.summary: Ukraine's Third Army Corps liberated 16 settlements and 277 square kilometers in Donetsk during Operation Vivaldi. RFE/RL journalists visited the newly secured frontline positions. They retraced the specific paths taken by Ukrainian infantry and assault troops during the military campaign. Ukraine's Third Army Corps liberated 16 settlements and 277 square kilometers in the Donetsk region during Operation Vivaldi. RFE/RL visits the frontline positions and retraces the path of the Ukrainian infantry and assault troops who took part in the military campaign.

articles.title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
articles.summary: COP31 delegates in Antalya launched a new global check on climate promise fulfillment. Ministers remain deadlocked over funding responsibilities and fossil fuel transition timelines. The core dispute centers on whether a greener future is just if poorer nations cannot afford the shift. With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can be called “just” if poorer countries cannot afford it.

articles.title: EU's $50 Billion Funding Push For Ukraine Caught In Budget Crossfire
articles.summary: The European Commission proposed a 45 billion euro loan for Ukraine on November 18. The funds aim to cover the country's 2027 financial shortfall. The plan now faces significant delays due to internal budget disputes within the bloc. The European Commission is putting forward a new 45-billion-euro ($50 billion) loan proposal for Ukraine on November 18, to cover a large part of the financial shortfall the war-torn country is facing for 2027.

articles.title: Xi’s APEC speech casts China as Asia’s open door as US closes
articles.summary: Xi Jinping addressed the APEC summit in Shenzhen, positioning China as an open alternative to US trade restrictions. He targeted Southeast Asian leaders and multinational executives, contrasting Washington's tariff deals and semiconductor controls with Beijing's stability. The speech aimed to secure economic partnerships without directly naming the United States. Taking the podium first at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Chinese President Xi Jinping responded to Washington’s transactional tariff deals, revived Quad security alignment and tightening semiconductor controls with a calculated counter-pitch aimed squarely at wavering Southeast Asian capitals and multinational executives.

articles.title: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
articles.summary: A survey of 195 organizations across 68 countries reveals that diversified funding strategies failed to protect civil society groups from the global aid retreat. The crisis extends beyond immediate financial shortfalls, indicating deeper structural vulnerabilities. Organizations that spent years building varied revenue streams are still facing severe operational challenges and instability. A survey of 195 organisations across more than 68 countries shows how the global aid retreat is hitting organizations that spent years building diverse funding streams.

The low-level fighting continued despite diplomatic efforts to secure a peace deal. US and Iranian forces exchanged tit-for-tat air strikes in the Middle East, while Gulf nations issued fresh warnings to residents amid threats of incoming projectiles as the currently low-level conflict continued to brew despite the efforts of regional mediators.

articles.summary: Ukraine struck the Crimean bridge, severing the peninsula's only direct road and rail link to the mainland. The attack occurred overnight on November 17. Russia retaliated by damaging two key bridges in Kyiv. Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov stated the campaign is just beginning. Ukraine has released video of its overnight strikes that damaged the bridge between the mainland and Russian-occupied Crimea, the only direct road and rail link to the peninsula.

articles.title: How the news scramble is messing with Bank of Japan policymaking
articles.summary: Japan's traditional shared media environment has eroded over three decades. Major newspapers and broadcast networks no longer dominate public discourse. This fragmentation complicates the Bank of Japan's ability to gauge market sentiment and manage monetary policy effectively. For the past three decades, Japanese society still enjoyed something close to a shared media life. Major newspapers had enormous circulation. NHK and a handful of commercial networks dominated television.

articles.title: Trump turns brief Manila stop into pre-Shenzhen leverage haul
articles.summary: Trump used his brief Manila stop to secure leverage before heading to Shenzhen. He arrived after the ASEAN plenary had already concluded. The compressed schedule was initially viewed as a diplomatic slight. He leveraged the visit to negotiate terms ahead of his China meeting. When US President Donald Trump touched down in Manila on Tuesday afternoon (November 17), arriving only after the Association of Southeast Asian Nations had already concluded its formal plenary and handed its rotating chair to Singapore, early international coverage largely framed the compressed 24 hour visit as a diplomatic slight.

articles.title: Ebola cases double in DR Congo, chemical exposure starts before birth, Türk concern over EU-Rwanda
articles.summary: The World Health Organization reported that Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have more than doubled in three months. Over 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths are now confirmed. The outbreak spans 67 health zones across eight provinces. The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has more than doubled in three months, with more than 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths now reported in 67 health zones across eight provinces, the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
articles.summary: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine reported that 2026 civilian casualties already exceed all previous years since the February 2022 invasion. The toll has risen dramatically compared to prior periods. This marks the highest recorded civilian death rate of the conflict to date. This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Singapore’s AI balancing act exposes ASEAN’s split-stack dilemma
articles.summary: Singapore signed the San Francisco Declaration on secure AI foundations on November 15. This move highlights the difficulty of balancing US and Chinese tech ties. Southeast Asian nations face a split-stack dilemma. They must maintain access to American computing while keeping commercial links with China. Singapore’s diplomatic maneuvers in Manila this week illustrate the increasingly difficult technology-balancing act facing Southeast Asia: maintaining access to American advanced computing infrastructure while preserving commercial engagement with China.

articles.title: Iranian Top Cleric Visits Bosnia As Tehran Seeks Opening To Europe
articles.summary: A senior Iranian cleric who briefly assumed supreme leader powers after Khamenei's death visited Sarajevo. He urged European nations to distance themselves from US and Israeli policies toward Tehran. The visit highlights Tehran's effort to cultivate a European diplomatic connection. A senior Iranian cleric who briefly helped exercise the powers of Iran's supreme leader following the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has visited Sarajevo, urging European countries to distance themselves from US and Israeli policies toward Tehran.

articles.summary: उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनाव में सीटों के बंटवारे पर सपा ने स्पष्ट रुख अपनाया है। पार्टी पिछली बार जीती सभी सीटें नहीं छोड़ेगी। कांग्रेस के 181 सीटों के दावे को सपा ने नकार दिया है। दोनों दलों के बीच सहयोग की शर्तें अभी तय नहीं हुई हैं। उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनाव में सीटों के बंटवारे को लेकर भले ही कांग्रेस 181 सीटों और सम्मान की लड़ाई के बड़े दावे कर रही हो लेकिन समाजवादी पार्टी की ओर से साफ कर दिया गया है कि पार्टी पिछली बार जीती कोई सीट नहीं छोड़ेगी।

articles.summary: अमेरिका और वेनेजुएला के बीच सैन्य सहयोग समझौता हुआ है। रक्षा मंत्री हेगसेथ ने प्रशिक्षण और खुफिया जानकारी साझा करने की पुष्टि की है। यह समझौता दोनों देशों के बीच सुरक्षा संबंधों को मजबूत करेगा। क्षेत्रीय स्थिरता के लिए यह कदम महत्वपूर्ण माना जा रहा है। वेनेजुएला और अमेरिका के बीच सैन्य समझौता: हेगसेथ बोले- प्रशिक्षण से लेकर खुफिया जानकारी तक करेंगे।
